result.title: Pro$^2$ Agent: Scientific Problem Probing for Autonomous AI R&D
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can now autonomously conduct AI research by writing code and running experiments. They typically do so by iteratively optimizing a codebase, while ignoring the problem structure behind the task. This formulation is effective on simpler tasks, but on difficult problems it often gets stuck in the wrong solution region because the agent never explicitly represents its understanding of the problem. We introduce Pro$^2$ Agent, which shifts the primary state of autonomous AI research from a codebase state to a Problem State: an explicit structure of what problems prevent success and which solutions are likely to address them. Pro$^2$ Agent initializes the Problem State through comprehensive analysis of available resources and constraints. It then performs targeted research to relate the identified problems to candidate solutions. Through controlled hypothesis testing, the agent updates the importance of a suspected problem or the benefit brought by a candidate solution. On the complete MLE-Bench, Pro$^2$ Agent matches the best reported medal rate (70.7%) under the standard 24-hour budget and reaches 76.0% with a 48-hour budget, the highest medal rate reported on the complete benchmark. It also achieves competitive performance on PostTrainBench. In addition, it produces research notes for each task that make the research process transparent and reusable by human researchers.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Pro² Agent，将自主 AI 研发的主要状态从代码库状态转为显式的「问题状态」，即记录阻碍成功的问题及其候选解的结构，并通过受控假设检验更新问题重要性与候选解收益，在 MLE-Bench 等基准上取得较高奖牌率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其显式问题状态与假设检验式状态更新，可能与 LVR 中如何显式维护多个 latent 假设、按证据更新其权重并据此停止推理的问题同构，可供核查；但任务与视觉模态无直接关联，迁移仅属推测。
